title: 1977 Bridgeview plaza and trailer park operated by Sheldon and Darlene Hallett.t
description: Sheldon and Darlene Hallett wanted to create something meaningful for themselves and their teenagers, so they opened an RV trailer park and gift shop called Bridgeview Campground Gift and Handcraft Centre. After securing permits and meeting the requirement of ten electrical sites, they prepared a total of thirty sites, including a dumping station for dry camping, a popular choice at the time, and set up the gift shop. “We were naïve at first, thinking the gift shop should be stocked with camping gear, but soon realized that visitors wanted items made in New Brunswick. I eventually filled the shelves with local crafts, especially from artisans at the Mactaquac craft fair. Ice was another constant need. Most nights, we wouldn’t get home until 11 p.m., after preparing countless trays of ice for the next day, until we could finally afford an ice machine. People came from everywhere, some flying into Montreal from as far away as Germany. It always amazed us where our visitors came from. We opened on Victoria Day and closed at Thanksgiving, eventually selling to Lona Pelkey in 1978. Just thinking about those days makes me happy,” smiled Darlene Hallett. (Photo courtesy of Darlene Hallett)
